QF.id: III-C Prevention of Money Laundering Act_35

question.text: Under PMLA, identity records of clients must be maintained for 5 years after the business relationship ends. If an intermediary opened a client account on April 1, 2015, and the account was closed on March 31, 2020, until what date must the identity records be preserved?

explanation.text: The Logic: Identity and account-file records must be maintained for five years after the business relationship has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later (NISM-Series-III-C workbook, pp.161 and 172). Account closed on March 31, 2020 plus five years gives March 31, 2025. The Trap: Adding five years to the account-opening date or using April 1 / 2027 endpoints ignores the source rule that the clock starts at account closure. Note: Page 172 also notes that records linked to an ongoing investigation are retained until the case is closed, so check for any open investigation before disposing of records.
